verses.kjv: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.modern: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
verses.modern: "Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher, "vanity of vanities; all is vanity."

verses.kjv: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
verses.modern: What does a man gain from all his labor at which he works under the sun?

verses.kjv: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
verses.modern: One generation passes away, and another generation comes, but the earth remains forever.

verses.kjv: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
verses.modern: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries back to the place where it rose.

verses.kjv: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
verses.modern: The wind goes toward the south and turns about to the north. It whirls about continually, and the wind returns again on its circuits.

verses.kjv: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
verses.modern: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place from which the rivers come, there they return again.

verses.kjv: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.modern: All things are full of labor; a man cannot put it into words. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

verses.kjv: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
verses.modern: That which has been is what shall be, and that which is done is what shall be done. There is no new thing under the sun.

verses.kjv: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
verses.modern: Is there anything of which it may be said, "See, this is new"? It has already been in ancient times, which were before us.

verses.kjv: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
verses.modern: There is no memory of former things, nor will there be any memory of things to come among those who come after.

verses.kjv: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.modern: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
verses.modern: I set my heart to seek and search out by wisdom all things that are done under heaven. This heavy task God has given to the sons of man, to be busy with.

verses.kjv: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and all is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
verses.modern: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

verses.kjv: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
verses.modern: I spoke with my own heart, saying, "I have come to greatness and have gained more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge."

verses.kjv: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: I set my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I saw that this also is vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
verses.modern: For in much wisdom is much grief, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.

chapters.summary: The Preacher declares that all is vanity and that there is nothing new under the sun. He introduces himself as king over Israel in Jerusalem and recounts how he set his heart to search out all things by wisdom, finding that even wisdom itself brings grief and sorrow.

verses.kjv: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity.
verses.modern: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with mirth, so enjoy pleasure." But this also was vanity.

verses.kjv: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
verses.modern: I said of laughter, "It is mad," and of mirth, "What does it accomplish?"

verses.kjv: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
verses.modern: I sought in my heart to give myself to wine, while my heart still guided me with wisdom, and to take hold of folly. I wanted to see what was good for the sons of men to do under heaven all the days of their life.

verses.kjv: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:
verses.modern: I made great works for myself. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.

verses.kjv: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
verses.modern: I made gardens and orchards for myself, and I planted in them trees of every kind of fruit.

verses.kjv: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:
verses.modern: I made pools of water for myself, to water the woods that brought forth trees.

verses.kjv: I got me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
verses.modern: I obtained menservants and maidservants, and I had servants born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.

verses.kjv: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
verses.modern: I also gathered for myself silver and gold, and the special treasure of kings and provinces. I obtained men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, with musical instruments of all kinds.

verses.kjv: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.modern: So I became great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.

verses.kjv: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.
verses.modern: Whatever my eyes desired, I did not keep from them. I withheld my heart from no joy, for my heart rejoiced in all my labor. This was my portion of all my labor.

verses.kjv: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
verses.modern: Then I looked on all the works my hands had done, and on the labor I had toiled to do. All was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.

verses.kjv: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.
verses.modern: Then I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly. For what can the man do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.

verses.kjv: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
verses.modern: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.

verses.kjv: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
verses.modern: The wise man's eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also saw that one event happens to them all.

verses.kjv: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
verses.modern: Then I said in my heart, "As it happens to the fool, so it happens even to me. Why then was I more wise?" Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.

verses.kjv: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.
verses.modern: For there is no lasting memory of the wise more than of the fool, since in the days to come all will be forgotten. And how does the wise man die? Just like the fool.

verses.kjv: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For all is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: Yea, I hated all my labour wherein I had laboured under the sun: seeing that I must leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
verses.modern: I hated all my labor at which I had worked under the sun, seeing that I must leave it to the man who will come after me.

verses.kjv: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
verses.modern: And who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all my labor at which I have worked and shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.

verses.kjv: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
verses.modern: So I turned to make my heart despair of all the labor at which I had worked under the sun.

verses.kjv: For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.modern: For there is a man whose labor is done with wisdom, knowledge, and fairness, yet he must leave it as a portion to a man who has not labored in it. This also is vanity and a great evil.

verses.kjv: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?
verses.modern: For what does a man have from all his labor and from the vexation of his heart, at which he has labored under the sun?

verses.kjv: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
verses.modern: For all his days are sorrows, and his work is grief. Even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.

verses.kjv: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
verses.modern: There is nothing better for a man than to eat and drink, and to let his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.

verses.kjv: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?
verses.modern: For who can eat, or who can enjoy it, more than I?

verses.kjv: For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: For God gives to the man who is good in his sight wisdom, knowledge, and joy. But to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and heaping up, that he may give it to the one who is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

chapters.summary: The Preacher tests himself with pleasure, laughter, wine, great building projects, wealth, and every delight, and concludes that all of it is vanity and vexation of spirit. He observes that the wise man and the fool share the same death, and that the only good is to eat, drink, and find enjoyment in one's labor as a gift from God.

verses.kjv: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
verses.modern: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under heaven:

verses.kjv: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
verses.modern: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pull up what is planted;

verses.kjv: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.modern: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to tear down, and a time to build up;

verses.kjv: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.modern: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.kjv: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.modern: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

verses.kjv: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.modern: a time to gain, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;

verses.kjv: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.modern: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silent, and a time to speak;

verses.kjv: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
verses.modern: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

verses.kjv: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?
verses.modern: What profit has the worker from that in which he labors?

verses.kjv: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of man to be exercised in it.
verses.modern: I have seen the task that God has given to the sons of man, to be busy with.

verses.kjv: He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
verses.modern: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set the world in their heart, yet no man can find out the work that God makes from the beginning to the end.

verses.kjv: I know that there is no good in them, but to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
verses.modern: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in their life.

verses.kjv: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.
verses.modern: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor — it is the gift of God.

verses.kjv: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.
verses.modern: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it. God does it so that men should fear before Him.

verses.kjv: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
verses.modern: That which has been is now, and that which is to be has already been. And God requires what is past.

verses.kjv: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
verses.modern: Moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, and wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, and iniquity was there.

verses.kjv: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
verses.modern: I said in my heart, "God shall judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work."

verses.kjv: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
verses.modern: I said in my heart concerning the state of the sons of men, that God might test them, and that they might see they themselves are like beasts.

verses.kjv: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
verses.modern: For what happens to the sons of men also happens to beasts; one thing happens to them both. As one dies, so dies the other. They all have one breath, so that a man has no advantage over a beast, for all is vanity.

verses.kjv: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
verses.modern: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.

verses.kjv: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?
verses.modern: Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth?

verses.kjv: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
verses.modern: So I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his own works, for that is his portion. For who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

chapters.summary: The Preacher declares that there is a time for everything — a time to be born and a time to die, a time to weep and a time to laugh. He observes that God has made everything beautiful in its time and set eternity in the hearts of men, yet no one can find out the full work of God. He notes that man and beast share the same breath and the same death, and all return to dust.

verses.kjv: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
verses.modern: So I returned and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun. I saw the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter. On the side of their oppressors there was power, but they had no comforter.

verses.kjv: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
verses.modern: Therefore I praised the dead who were already dead more than the living who are still alive.

verses.kjv: Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.modern: And better than them both is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

verses.kjv: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: Again I considered all labor and every skillful work, and saw that for this a man is envied by his neighbor. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
verses.modern: The fool folds his hands together and eats his own flesh.

verses.kjv: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: Better is a handful with quietness than both hands full with labor and vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
verses.modern: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

verses.kjv: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
verses.modern: There is one alone, without a second; he has neither child nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his labor, nor is his eye satisfied with riches. Nor does he ask, "For whom do I labor, and deprive my soul of good?" This also is vanity; it is a heavy task.

verses.kjv: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
verses.modern: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.

verses.kjv: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
verses.modern: For if they fall, the one will lift up his companion. But woe to him who is alone when he falls, for he has no one to help him up.

verses.kjv: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
verses.modern: Again, if two lie together, they have warmth. But how can one be warm alone?

verses.kjv: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.modern: And if one prevails against him, two shall withstand him. A threefold cord is not quickly broken.

verses.kjv: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
verses.modern: Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no longer take warning.

verses.kjv: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.
verses.modern: For out of prison he comes to reign, while he who is born in his kingdom becomes poor.

verses.kjv: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
verses.modern: I considered all the living who walk under the sun, along with the second child who shall stand up in his place.

verses.kjv: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: There is no end of all the people, of all who were before them. Yet those who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

chapters.summary: The Preacher considers the oppressions done under the sun and sees that the oppressed have no comforter. He observes that all labor and skillful work spring from envy, that two are better than one, and that a threefold cord is not quickly broken. He notes that even a poor wise child is better than an old foolish king.

verses.kjv: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
verses.modern: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Be more ready to hear than to offer the sacrifice of fools, for they do not consider that they do evil.

verses.kjv: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
verses.modern: Do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be quick to utter anything before God. For God is in heaven and you on earth, therefore let your words be few.

verses.kjv: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice is known by multitude of words.
verses.modern: For a dream comes through much business, and a fool's voice is known by many words.

verses.kjv: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
verses.modern: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, for He has no pleasure in fools. Pay what you have vowed.

verses.kjv: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
verses.modern: It is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.

verses.kjv: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
verses.modern: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?

verses.kjv: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.
verses.modern: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also various vanities. But fear God.

verses.kjv: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
verses.modern: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent perversion of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel at the matter. For he who is higher than the highest regards it, and there are higher ones over them.

verses.kjv: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
verses.modern: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king himself is served by the field.

verses.kjv: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
verses.modern: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with increase. This also is vanity.

verses.kjv: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
verses.modern: When goods increase, those who eat them increase. And what good is there for the owners, except to behold them with their eyes?

verses.kjv: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.modern: The sleep of a working man is sweet, whether he eats little or much. But the abundance of the rich will not let him sleep.

verses.kjv: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
verses.modern: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: riches kept for their owners to their own hurt.

verses.kjv: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
verses.modern: But those riches perish through misfortune, and he fathers a son, and there is nothing in his hand.

verses.kjv: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.modern: As he came forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he return, going as he came. He shall take nothing from his labor that he can carry away in his hand.

verses.kjv: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
verses.modern: And this also is a grievous evil: in every way as he came, so shall he go. And what profit has he who has labored for the wind?

verses.kjv: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
verses.modern: All his days he also eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow, sickness, and wrath.

verses.kjv: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it is his portion.
verses.modern: This is what I have seen: it is good and fitting for one to eat and drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor at which he works under the sun all the days of his life that God gives Him. For this is His portion.

verses.kjv: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.
verses.modern: And every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and given Him power to eat from them, to take His portion and to rejoice in His labor — this is the gift of God.

verses.kjv: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth him in the joy of his heart.
verses.modern: For he shall not much remember the days of his life, because God keeps Him busy with the joy of His heart.

chapters.summary: The Preacher warns against rash words before God and urges that vows be paid promptly. He observes that the lover of money is never satisfied, that riches kept bring harm to their owner, and that a man leaves the world as naked as he entered it. He concludes that it is good and fitting to eat, drink, and enjoy one's labor, for this is God's gift.

verses.kjv: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
verses.modern: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:

verses.kjv: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
verses.modern: A man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that He lacks nothing for His soul of all that He desires, yet God does not give Him the power to enjoy them, but a stranger eats them. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

verses.kjv: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
verses.modern: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and he has no burial — I say that a stillborn child is better than he.

verses.kjv: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
verses.modern: For it comes in with vanity and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.

verses.kjv: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
verses.modern: Moreover it has not seen the sun, nor known anything. This has more rest than the other.

verses.kjv: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.modern: Indeed, though he lives a thousand years twice over, yet he has seen no good. Do not all go to one place?

verses.kjv: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.modern: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet his appetite is not filled.

verses.kjv: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
verses.modern: For what does the wise have more than the fool? What does the poor man have, who knows how to walk before the living?

verses.kjv: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.modern: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.kjv: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither can he contend with him that is mightier than he.
verses.modern: That which has been is named already, and it is known that it is man. He cannot contend with him who is mightier than he.

verses.kjv: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
verses.modern: Since there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better for it?

verses.kjv: For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
verses.modern: For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? Who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

chapters.summary: The Preacher describes the evil of a man to whom God gives wealth, honor, and everything he desires, yet God does not give him the power to enjoy it. He argues that a stillborn child is better off than such a man, and that no one knows what is good for man in the days of his vain life.

verses.kjv: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
verses.modern: A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

verses.kjv: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
verses.modern: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men, and the living will lay it to his heart.

verses.kjv: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
verses.modern: Sorrow is better than laughter, for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

verses.kjv: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.modern: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.

verses.kjv: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.modern: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.

verses.kjv: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.
verses.modern: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.

verses.kjv: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
verses.modern: Surely oppression drives a wise man mad, and a bribe destroys the heart.

verses.kjv: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.modern: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning, and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.

verses.kjv: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
verses.modern: Do not be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.

verses.kjv: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.
verses.modern: Do not say, "What is the cause that the former days were better than these?" For you do not inquire wisely about this.

verses.kjv: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
verses.modern: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and by it there is profit to those who see the sun.

verses.kjv: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
verses.modern: For wisdom is a defense, and money is a defense; but the excellence of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who have it.

verses.kjv: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?
verses.modern: Consider the work of God, for who can make straight what He has made crooked?

verses.kjv: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
verses.modern: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God has set the one over against the other, so that man should find nothing of what shall be after Him.

verses.kjv: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness.
verses.modern: All things I have seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness.

verses.kjv: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
verses.modern: Do not be overly righteous, nor make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

verses.kjv: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
verses.modern: Do not be overly wicked, nor be a fool. Why should you die before your time?

verses.kjv: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
verses.modern: It is good that you should take hold of this, and also from the other do not withdraw your hand. For he who fears God shall come forth from them all.

verses.kjv: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
verses.modern: Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten mighty men who are in the city.

verses.kjv: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
verses.modern: For there is not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin.

verses.kjv: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
verses.modern: Also do not take to heart every word that is spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you.

verses.kjv: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
verses.modern: For often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.

verses.kjv: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
verses.modern: All this I have proved by wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was far from me.

verses.kjv: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
verses.modern: That which is far off and exceedingly deep — who can find it out?

verses.kjv: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
verses.modern: I applied my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness.

verses.kjv: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
verses.modern: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands are like bands. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her.

verses.kjv: Behold, this have I found, saith the Preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
verses.modern: "See, this I have found," says the Preacher, "counting one by one to find out the account,

verses.kjv: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
verses.modern: which my soul still seeks, but I have not found. One man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all those I have not found.

verses.kjv: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
verses.modern: This only I have found: that God has made man upright, but they have sought out many inventions."

chapters.summary: The Preacher offers proverbs on wisdom: a good name is better than precious ointment, sorrow is better than laughter, and the patient in spirit is better than the proud. He warns against being overly righteous or overly wicked and observes that there is not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin. He concludes that God made man upright, but men have sought out many inventions.

verses.kjv: Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
verses.modern: Who is like the wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.

verses.kjv: I counsel thee to keep the king's commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
verses.modern: I counsel you to keep the king's commandment, because of the oath of God.

verses.kjv: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.
verses.modern: Do not be hasty to go out of his presence. Do not persist in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him.

verses.kjv: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.modern: Where the word of a king is, there is power, and who may say to him, "What are you doing?"

verses.kjv: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment.
verses.modern: Whoever keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing, and a wise man's heart discerns both time and judgment.

verses.kjv: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.
verses.modern: Because for every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.

verses.kjv: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
verses.modern: For he does not know what shall be, for who can tell him when it shall be?

verses.kjv: There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
verses.modern: No man has power over the spirit to retain the spirit, nor has He power in the day of death. There is no discharge in that war, nor shall wickedness deliver those who are given to it.

verses.kjv: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
verses.modern: All this I have seen, and applied my heart to every work that is done under the sun. There is a time when one man rules over another to his own hurt.

verses.kjv: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
verses.modern: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This also is vanity.

verses.kjv: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.modern: Because sentence against an evil work is not carried out speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

verses.kjv: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
verses.modern: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with those who fear God, Who fear before Him.

verses.kjv: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
verses.modern: But it shall not be well with the wicked, nor shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God.

verses.kjv: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
verses.modern: There is a vanity that is done on the earth: there are just men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.

verses.kjv: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
verses.modern: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat and to drink and to be merry. For this shall remain with him from his labor the days of his life, which God gives Him under the sun.

verses.kjv: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
verses.modern: When I applied my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on the earth — for there is one who neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes —

verses.kjv: Then I beheld all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yea further; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
verses.modern: then I saw all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. Though a man labors to seek it out, yet he shall not find it. And though a wise man thinks to know it, yet He shall not be able to find it.

chapters.summary: The Preacher counsels obedience to the king and observes that no man has power over the day of death. He notes that because sentence against evil is not carried out quickly, men are emboldened to sin, yet he knows it shall be well with those who fear God. He concludes that no man can find out all the work of God, no matter how hard he searches.

verses.kjv: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them.
verses.modern: For all this I considered in my heart, to declare all this: that the righteous and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God. No man knows either love or hatred by all that is before them.

verses.kjv: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
verses.modern: All things come alike to all: one event happens to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good and to the clean and to the unclean, to him who sacrifices and to him who does not sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; and he who swears, so is he who fears an oath.

verses.kjv: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
verses.modern: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun: that one event happens to all. Indeed, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

verses.kjv: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.modern: For to him who is joined to all the living there is hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

verses.kjv: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.modern: For the living know that they shall die, but the dead know nothing. They have no more a reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.

verses.kjv: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
verses.modern: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy have now perished. Nor have they any more a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.

verses.kjv: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
verses.modern: Go your way, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart, for God now accepts your works.

verses.kjv: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.
verses.modern: Let your garments always be white, and let your head lack no ointment.

verses.kjv: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
verses.modern: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity. For that is your portion in this life, and in your labor at which you work under the sun.

verses.kjv: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
verses.modern: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might, for there is no work, nor planning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in the grave, where you are going.

verses.kjv: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
verses.modern: I returned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.

verses.kjv: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
verses.modern: For man also does not know his time. Like the fish that are taken in a cruel net, and like the birds that are caught in the snare, so are the sons of men snared in an evil time when it falls suddenly upon them.

verses.kjv: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me:
verses.modern: This wisdom I have also seen under the sun, and it seemed great to me:

verses.kjv: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
verses.modern: There was a little city, and few men within it. A great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.

verses.kjv: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.modern: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city. Yet no man remembered that same poor man.

verses.kjv: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.modern: Then I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." Nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

verses.kjv: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
verses.modern: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him who rules among fools.

verses.kjv: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
verses.modern: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

chapters.summary: The Preacher observes that one event — death — happens to all alike, to the righteous and the wicked. He urges men to eat, drink, and enjoy life with the wife they love, for there is no work or wisdom in the grave. He notes that the race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, and that wisdom, though better than weapons of war, is often despised.

verses.kjv: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
verses.modern: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking smell. So does a little folly to him who has a reputation for wisdom and honor.

verses.kjv: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.
verses.modern: A wise man's heart is at his right hand, but a fool's heart at his left.

verses.kjv: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
verses.modern: And also, when he who is a fool walks by the way, his wisdom fails him, and he tells everyone that he is a fool.

verses.kjv: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
verses.modern: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for yielding pacifies great offenses.

verses.kjv: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
verses.modern: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, like an error that proceeds from the ruler:

verses.kjv: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.modern: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

verses.kjv: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.modern: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

verses.kjv: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.modern: He who digs a pit shall fall into it, and whoever breaks through a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

verses.kjv: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
verses.modern: Whoever moves stones shall be hurt by them, and he who splits wood shall be endangered by it.

verses.kjv: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
verses.modern: If the iron is blunt, and he does not sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength. But wisdom is profitable to direct.

verses.kjv: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
verses.modern: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment, and a babbler is no better.

verses.kjv: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.modern: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool swallow up himself.

verses.kjv: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
verses.modern: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness, and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

verses.kjv: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.modern: A fool also is full of words. A man cannot tell what shall be, and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

verses.kjv: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
verses.modern: The labor of fools wearies every one of them, because none of them knows how to go to the city.

verses.kjv: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
verses.modern: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, and your princes feast in the morning!

verses.kjv: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.modern: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat at the proper time, for strength and not for drunkenness!

verses.kjv: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
verses.modern: By much laziness the building decays, and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

verses.kjv: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
verses.modern: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes merry, but money answers all things.

verses.kjv: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
verses.modern: Do not curse the king, not even in your thought, and do not curse the rich in your bedchamber. For a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.

chapters.summary: The Preacher teaches that a little folly ruins a reputation for wisdom, just as dead flies spoil the ointment. He offers proverbs on rulers and fools: woe to the land whose king is a child, and blessed is the land whose king is the son of nobles. He warns that even a secret curse against the king may be carried by a bird of the air.

verses.kjv: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
verses.modern: Cast your bread upon the waters, for you shall find it after many days.

verses.kjv: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.modern: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, for you do not know what evil shall come upon the earth.

verses.kjv: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
verses.modern: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth. And if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.

verses.kjv: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
verses.modern: He who watches the wind shall not sow, and he who regards the clouds shall not reap.

verses.kjv: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
verses.modern: As you do not know the way of the spirit, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, even so you do not know the works of God Who makes all things.

verses.kjv: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.modern: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which shall prosper, either this or that, or whether both shall be equally good.

verses.kjv: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
verses.modern: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.

verses.kjv: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
verses.modern: But if a man lives many years and rejoices in them all, yet let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.

verses.kjv: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.modern: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes. But know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

verses.kjv: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
verses.modern: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for childhood and youth are vanity.

chapters.summary: The Preacher urges generosity — cast your bread upon the waters — and diligence in labor, for no man knows what disaster may come. He counsels the young man to rejoice in his youth and walk in the ways of his heart, but warns that God will bring every action into judgment.

verses.kjv: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.modern: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near when you shall say, "I have no pleasure in them";

verses.kjv: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
verses.modern: while the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars are not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain;

verses.kjv: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
verses.modern: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows grow dim;

verses.kjv: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
verses.modern: when the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;

verses.kjv: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.modern: also when they shall be afraid of what is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets.

verses.kjv: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
verses.modern: Remember him — before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

verses.kjv: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
verses.modern: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was, and the spirit shall return to God Who gave it.

verses.kjv: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all is vanity.
verses.modern: "Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher, "all is vanity."

verses.kjv: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.modern: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. He gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

verses.kjv: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
verses.modern: The Preacher sought to find acceptable words, and what was written was upright — even words of truth.

verses.kjv: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.modern: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails firmly fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.

verses.kjv: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.modern: And further, my son, be warned by these: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

verses.kjv: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.modern: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.

verses.kjv: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.modern: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil.

chapters.summary: The Preacher urges the young to remember their Creator before old age comes, describing the decline of the body in vivid metaphor — the keepers of the house tremble, the grinders cease, and the silver cord is loosed. He repeats his verdict that all is vanity and delivers the conclusion of the whole matter: fear God and keep His commandments, for God shall bring every work into judgment.
